brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Build has 4 bases across two levels: piece:0,0,0;full + piece:0,1,0;half-n at level 0, and piece:0,0,1;full + piece:0,1,1;half-n at level 1 (snap connectors + jointBolt:0#0,0#5 and jointBolt:1#0,0#5); top closed with cover:0,0,1;full;top and cover:0,1,1;half-n;top; overall height 160mm, footprint ~220x374mm; meshClash clear, check_build ok.
Two drawers installed: drawer:0#0,1#cut at 0,1,0 (level 0) and drawer:1#0,1#cut at 0,1,1 (level 1), both on the half-n cut faces (key s), operable open/close.

Capped open faces (11 caps) and locked joints; flat top deck (f19/f87 across two covers) staged with tape measure, parts-tray and multimeter to show workbench storage purpose. 3D-printed plastic not load-rated - configurator checks fit only.

finish.summary: Two-storey tower built from 4 bases (full+half-n per level) with two drawers, one per storey. Top covers provide work surface, joints locked and open faces capped. Staged with workshop props; check_build ok and meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
